one_liner: Intercom has a REST API at api.intercom.io with OAuth 2.0 (authorization-code) for public apps and static Access Tokens for private apps. A free US-only developer workspace is available. Public apps need Intercom review. No vendor MCP server is evidenced in the supplied pages.
auth_notes: OAuth is required for apps that access other people's data, and it is a standard authorization-code exchange. Access Tokens are used for private apps on your own workspace and are sent as a bearer token. The pages do not say whether OAuth tokens expire or have refresh tokens.
access_notes: A free development workspace gives Developer Hub access, where you can set up OAuth and webhooks. It is US-only and limited. A third-party guide says API access is on every plan, but Intercom's own pages do not confirm this. Intercom's own product has a 14-day free trial.
blocker_notes: Private-app tokens need no review. A public OAuth app that any customer can install must be submitted to Intercom for review. The dev workspace is US-only and limited. Composio lists an 'Intercom MCP' toolkit, but nothing on the pages shows it is vendor-published, so it is not counted as official.
